That night, when his friend came for me again, phone in hand to record "You brought this ruin on us!" she shrieked. "Go die, Ariana! Just die!" Her curse was the final blow.

Chapter 1 Ariana Mcneil POV Five years ago, on my wedding night, my new husband, Dorian Miller, drugged me and left me ina room with his best friend, Blake Dominguez That single act of calculated betrayal ignited a war that would ultimately consume us all. | was Ariana Mcneil, a name synonymous with D.C. influence daughter of a powerful political dynasty.

Dorian, a brilliant Department of Justice attorney from a less prominent background, married me not for love, but for revenge. He believed my family destroyed his, and this marriage was his weapon. | woke up disoriented, the room spinning My vision blurred. A heavy weight pressed down on me. Blake Dominguez, Dorian's closest friend from law school, leered above me. His breath smelled of stale whiskey and something foul. He was a large man, his muscles straining against his tailored suit, his eyes dark with predatory intent. Panic seized my throat, a silent scream trapped behind my lips.

| thrashed, my limbs heavy and useless. He pinned my wrists above my head with one hand, his other ripping at my wedding gown. Tears streamed down my face, hot and humiliating | begged, pleaded, my voice a weak croak, but his face remained a mask of cruel amusement The night stretched into an eternity of terror and helplessness. By morning the city buzzed with the scandal. A grainy video, clearly doctored to frame me, circulated online. It showed me in a compromising position with Blake, shattering my reputation, mocking my family's name. The world watched, judged, and condemned me.

Dorian appeared in the doorway of my bedroom later that day. His face was a mask of cold fury, his eyes devoid of any warmth | might have once imagined. He saw the bruises on my arms, the tear tracks on my face, but his expression did not soften. "You disgraced me, Ariana," Dorian said, his voice flat, devoid of emotion. "You embarrassed my name, my position." He stepped closer, his shadow falling over me. | flinched. "Your father's ambition ruined my family," he continued, his words like ice shards.

"You will pay for his sins." He accused me of orchestrating the entire event, of seducing Blake. | stared at him, my throat raw, my heart a raw wound. | did not speak. There was no point. His eyes held only hatred. | turned my back on him. | focused on putting one foot in front of the other, walking away from the shattered remnants of my wedding day. That day marked the beginning of a brutal, five-year war. Dorian systematically dismantled my family's empire.

My father, once a titan of industry and politics, found himself ensnared in a web of legal battles, eventually imprisoned on trumped-up charges. My older brother, James, a rising star in the military, died in a "training accident" overseas, a casualty | knew, in my gut, Dorian had a hand in. My mother, Frances Montoya, a woman of grace and tradition, watched her world crumble. The loss of her husband and son broke her. She suffered a complete mental breakdown, her mind fracturing under the weight of grief and despair. The family institutionalizedher. | fought back, fiercely, desperately.

| used every connection, every bit of cunning | possessed, to sabotage Dorian's career. | leaked sensitive information about his cases, discredited him in the media, and created legal obstacles at every turn. He faced public humiliation formal investigations, and stalled promotions. There were moments when he teetered on the brink of professional ruin, his carefully constructed career threatening to collapse. Each time, a fleeting, bitter satisfaction filled me. Our conflict became a twisted dance of destruction, each blow exchanged leaving deeper scars on us both.

Our marriage was a battlefield, our home a cage. My love for him, a secret | had cherished for years before our arranged marriage, had long since curdled into a potent, all-consuming hatred. Then came the day | visited my mother for the last time. Her eyes, once vibrant, were vacant, her hair disheveled. She sat in a sterile room at the institution staring blankly ahead. When she saw me, her face twisted in rage. She lunged, her frail hands scratching at my face. "You!" she shrieked, her voice hoarse and broken. "You provoked him!

You brought this ruin upon us all!" She clawed at my skin, leaving angry red marks. Her words cut deeper than any physical wound. "Go die, Ariana! Just die!" she screamed, her eyes wide with madness. "You deserve nothing less!" Her words, the final blow, echoed in the hollow space of my soul. | had lost everything. My father was gone, James was gone, and now my mother hated me, wishing me dead. The will to live drained from me completely. | had hidden a small, potent bottle of pills for months. | reached into my pocket, my fingers brushing against the cold glass. | knew then it was time.

Time to obey my mother's curse. But not yet. There was one last thing! had to do. That same evening, Dorian returned home. He was a storm of raw anger. He found me inthe livingroom, staring out the window at the city lights. He grabbed my arm, his grip bruising He pulled me into the bedroom, his eyes blazing. He shoved me onto the bed, then leaned over me, his lips assaulting mine. His kiss was brutal, tasting of aggression and resentment. | felt the faint, cloying scent of another woman's perfume on his skin, floral and sweet, a stark contrast to the bitterness of his touch.

My heart, long since numb, ached with a dull, familiar pain. He pulled back slightly, his eyes burning into mine. "Still playing the victim, Ariana?" he snarled, his voice low and contemptuous. "Still trying to make me regret what happened on our wedding night?" He continued to press down on me, his body a heavy weight. | felt nothing only a profound weariness. My eyes welled up, but he did not stop. He tore at my dress, the fabric ripping with a harsh sound. "Submit, Ariana. Just submit," he demanded. | lay still, my body limp. My compliance surprised him.

He paused, his brow furrowed in confusion, a flicker of something unreadable in his eyes. "What is this act now?" he asked, his voice laced with suspicion. "Trying a new trick?" He still believed | was capable of endless manipulation He still saw me only as a reflection of my father, a scheming Mcneil. "Remember that night, Ariana?" he whispered, his voice dangerously soft. "The night you brought shame to us all. You enjoyed it, didn't you? The thrill of the scandal?" My tears flowed freely now, blurring his face.

| felt a wave of nausea, the other woman's perfume clinging to him, making my stomach churn. | knew Kinsley Hudson's scent well. She was the sweet, gentle daughter of Dorian's deceased mentor, a woman he felt a profound duty to protect. Kinsley had often appeared, seemingly by chance, at critical moments during our war, her innocent expressions and tearful accusations always turning Dorian further against me. She had mastered the art of playing the victim, and Dorian, blinded by a sense of obligation and his own hatred, always fell for it.

"Just finish it, Dorian," | said, my voice barely a whisper, flat and devoid of emotion. "| want to go home before it gets dark." My calm infuriated him. He grabbed my jaw, squeezing hard. "Still trying to play the innocent martyr?" he scoffed. "Still trying to manipulate me with your pathetic obedience?" He stood up abruptly, pulling his shirt straight. He tossed a small velvet box onto the bed. It struck my arm, a sharp, physical pain, a final insult. "Here," he said, his voice cold. "Consider this your compensation. A newtitle, a new status. Just accept your place." | did not move.

The box lay beside me, a meaningless trinket. "Your family brought this on themselves, Ariana," he said, his voice hardening. "You too. You had a chance to accept your fate, but you chose war. Now live with the consequences. You get nothing else from me." He slammed the door behind him, the sound echoing through the empty house. lreached for the small bottle hidden under my pillow. Its cold glass felt strangely comforting in my palm. My mother's words rang in my ears: "Go die, Ariana!" | looked at the bottle, then at the window where twilight painted the sky in somber hues.

chapters.title: Chapter 2
chapters.content:
Chapter 2 Ariana Mcneil POV The next morning, | carried a carefully wrapped gift to the institution It was a small, delicate box filled with osmanthus flowers, my mother's favorite. Their sweet, lingering fragrance always reminded her of our family garden, a place of peace before the war. Entering the facility required Dorian's explicit permission, a stark reminder of his control, even over my last goodbyes. The guards, stern-faced men in crisp uniforms, scrutinized my every move. They watched me unlock the heavy doors, each click a dull thud in the silence.

| found my mother in her usual chair, staring out the window. Her face was gaunt, her eyes distant. | forced a smile onto my lips, a painful mask. "Happy birthday, Mother," | said, my voice trembling slightly. She did not respond. Her gaze remained fixed on some unseen point beyond the glass. | bit back the wave of despair that threatened to engulf me. | knelt beside her chair, opening the box of osmanthus flowers. Their delicate scent filled the sterile room. "Look, Mother," | whispered, holding the box gently. "| picked them from the old garden. Just for you.

Do you remember?" | described the garden, the warmth of the sun, the bees buzzing among the flowers. Her eyes remained blank. "Just a small nod, Mother," | pleaded, my voice hoarse. "Just a flicker of recognition. Please." | knew this was my last visit. The pills in my pocket felt heavy, a cold promise. | needed some small comfort from her, a final crumb of love before | disappeared forever. Suddenly, her hand shot out, striking the box. Osmanthus flowers scattered across the floor. She grabbed my hair, her grip surprisingly strong, pulling my head down.

My face plunged into the scattered flowers, the soft petals pressing against my nose and mouth. Their sweet scent turned suffocating. "Get out!" she shrieked, her voice raw. "Get out, you witch! You ruined everything!" She pushed me, clawing at my face and neck. Her nails, surprisingly sharp, raked across my skin, leaving stinging trails. "Go die! Just like your brother!" she screamed, her voice rising to a hysterical pitch. "You killed him! You killed him with your stubborn fight against Dorian! He promised to care for Kinsley, not you! You didn't listen!

You deserve to die!" The flowers clogged my nostrils, making it hard to breathe. | choked, gasping for air, the sweet fragrance now a choking haze. | tried to speak, to reason, but her hands were everywhere, pushing pulling, scratching. She shoved me violently. My head struck the doorframe with a sickening thud. Pain exploded behind my eyes. "Get out! Get out!" she shrieked again, her voice echoing in the small room. Then, she leaned in, her eyes wide and frenzied. "Dorian loves Kinsley! He always did! You just stood in the way! You should have known your place!

He promised to protect her, not you!" she hissed, her breath hot on my face. "You ungrateful wretch! Go die! Go die!" Tears streamed down my face, mixing with the crushed petals and the stinging blood from my scratches. My hands trembled, not from fear, but from the profound desolation that settled over me. | remembered her gentle hands, petting my hair when | was a child. | remembered her stories, her laughter, her quiet strength. Now, only hatred radiated from her. She truly believed | was the villain, the cause of all her suffering. Had | truly been so wrong?

Had my fight, my stubborn refusal to break, truly destroyed everyone | loved? | looked at her, my voice raspy, barely audible. "Yes, Mother," | whispered, my eyes vacant. "I will. | will go die." A moment of silence fell over the room. My mother froze, catching my dead gaze. Her eyes, clouded by madness, seemed to clear for a split second, a flicker of something resembling fear. Then, the madness returned. She shoved me out of the room, slamming the door shut with a final, echoing bang. | stood outside her door for a long time, the pain in my head dulling, my body feeling strangely light.

My legs finally moved, carrying me slowly to the nearest restroom. | splashed cold water on my face, washing away the blood, the tears, the sticky residue of the crushed flowers. | looked at my reflection. A stranger stared back at me, hollow-eyed, bruised, and utterly empty. The marriage, the war, the losses -it had all been a terrible, unforgivable mistake. Tonight, | would end it. For good.

chapters.title: Chapter 3
chapters.content:
Chapter 3 Ariana Mcneil POV | left the institution the sky opening up above me in a sudden, torrential downpour. Rain lashed down, soaking my thin clothes instantly. | walked aimlessly, the cold water chilling me to the bone, but | felt nothing. The physical discomfort was a distant hum against the deafening silence in my mind. Every drop that hit me felt like a cleansing, washing away the last remnants of my will to fight. Just as suddenly as it began, the rain stopped. Dorian stood before me, a black umbrella held aloft, his dark suit clinging to his frame, damp in places.

His eyes were unreadable, a complex mix of anger and something else | couldn't decipher. He had been watching me, | realized. He grabbed my arm, his grip hard, and pulled me towards a nearby building, a high-end restaurant | recognized. | remembered seeing him through the window earlier, sitting in a private booth with Blake and Kinsley, their faces illuminated by the soft glow of the restaurant lights. He dragged me inside, his fingers digging into my flesh. The pain was sharp, but | remained silent. We entered the private booth.

The air was thick with the scent of expensive liquor and cigar smoke. Blake Dominguez, his eyes narrowed, smirked at me. "Look what the storm dragged in," Blake slurred, taking a swig from his glass. "The great Ariana Mcneil. Reduced to a drowned rat. How's Daddy dearest doing in prison? And your brother? Oh, wait. He's dead, isn't he?" Blake was Dorian's best friend from law school, a man who consistently rode Dorian's coattails, his arrogance fueled by Dorian's power. He was a sycophant, but also a cruel brute, a man whose casual cruelty had set the stage for my entire tragedy.

He reveled in my family's downfall, his eyes sweeping over my drenched form with undisguised contempt. "Still warm, | bet," Blake said, his gaze lingering indecently on my body. "Maybe a little warmth would do you good, eh?" A few of the other men in the booth chuckled, but the laughter died down quickly under Dorian's cold, steady gaze. Dorian lit a cigar, the smoke curling around his face, obscuring his expression. "Keep it civil," Dorian said, his voice low and dangerous, a warning. "Remember your decorum." His tone was that of a commander addressing his soldiers, firm and unwavering.

The men fell silent, their earlier bravado wilting under his stare. Blake, though visibly annoyed, merely grunted and averted his eyes. Dorian turned his attention to me, his brow furrowed. Before he could speak, Kinsley Hudson, slender and fair, emerged from behind him, wrapping her arms around his waist. She looked at me, a triumphant glint in her seemingly innocent eyes. "Oh, Ariana, darling, what happened to you?" Kinsley cooed, her voice saccharine sweet. "You look absolutely dreadful. Those men, they can be so crude.

Don't mind them." She turned to the others, her voice laced with feigned indignation "Honestly, how can you speak to Dorian's wife that way? Especially when I'm here. Dorian has always been so protective of me. You know how much my late father meant to him, and how he promised to look after me, right, darling?" She squeezed Dorian's arm, her head resting on his shoulder. "Perhaps you need a new outfit, dear. I'm sure Dorian wouldn't mind. He's always so generous with me." Dorian's hand gently stroked Kinsley's hair, a gesture of affection and reassurance | had never received from him.

A bitter realization settled in. My past acts of rebellion, my attempts to fight back, to assert my worth, now felt utterly meaningless. | had drained myself of all fight, all hope. | simply wanted it to end. | tried to leave, but Kinsley blocked my path. "Wait, Ariana," Kinsleysaid, "| have somethingfor you." She held out a delicate, antique silver locket. "This was my grandmother's. Dorian insists | keep it, but | feel you deserve it more, as Dorian's wife now, of course." She held it out to me, a smug smile playing on her lips. "It's a family heirloom.

Very precious." | reached for it, my fingers numb. The locket slipped from mv arasp, clattering to the hard floor. shattering into several pieces. Kinsley shrieked, then crumpled to the floor, collapsing into Dorian's arms. She began to sob, clutching at his shirt. "She pushed me, Dorian!" Kinsley cried, her voice muffled against his chest. "She pushed me and broke it! My grandmother's locket! It was so precious!" She looked up at him, her eyes brimming with tears, her lower lip trembling.

"My ankle, it hurts." | watched her performance, a masterclass in manipulation Dorian, as always, fell for it. His face hardened. He gently lifted Kinsley, cradling her in his arms. "Is your ankle alright?" he asked, his voice tender, full of concern. He turned his furious gaze on me. "What have you done now, Ariana?" Dorian growled, his voice low and menacing. "Apologize to Kinsley. Now." "How would you like me to apologize, Dorian?" | asked, my voice flat, empty of any emotion. "Should | kneel? Or perhaps offer my body to Blake again?

Would that suffice for breaking an heirloom?" My words hung in the air, cold and shocking. My past self, the proud, sharp-witted Ariana, would have raged, screamed, fought. But that Ariana was long dead. This current version of me felt nothing. Humiliation | realized, was a mere trifle when faced with the absolute certainty of my own demise. "Just tell me what you want, Dorian," | continued, my voice calm, almost detached. "I'm tired. | want to go home before nightfall." Dorian's eyes blazed with an intensity | hadn't seen before. He violently flung me away.

| stumbled back, my head hitting the wall with a dull thud. The room fell silent. Everyone stared, frozen in place. "Get out," Doriancommanded, his voice raw with fury. "All of you. Now." The men scrambled, quickly vacating the booth. Kinsley, still clutched in Dorian's arms, looked at me with a triumphant smirk before he carried her out. As he reached the door, Dorian paused. He looked back at me, and for the briefest moment, | saw something in his eyes that made my breath catch-not hatred, but something | had never seen before. Confusion. Or perhaps, fear. Then he disappeared.

Minutes later, my phone vibrated. A text message from Dorian. "Come home. We need to talk. | can explain everything." | looked at the message, a hollow laugh escaping my lips. Explain? After five years of calculated cruelty, after my family was destroyed, after my mother cursed me to die? | knew what explanation meant. It meant another manipulation another twist of the knife. He would never understand. | would not wait for him. | had made my decision. And by the time he got home, it would be too late. 88 Babe, here are your Free Coins! Check

chapters.content:
Chapter 4 Ariana Mcneil POV Dorian left. | remained alone in the hollow silence of the booth. My phone vibrated again with another message from him. | pulled it out, stared at his name, then, with a strange sense of finality, navigated to his contact and deleted him. All of his numbers, all of our message threads, erased. | walked out of the restaurant and hailed a cab to my apartment. The apartment felt cold, sterile, and empty. | began to pack, my movements robotic. | pulled open drawers, emptied closets, my fingers brushing against forgotten relics of a life that no longer existed.

Underneath a stack of old scarves, | found a bundle of letters, tied with a faded ribbon. My breath hitched. They were my letters, written years ago, a testament to a girl | barely recognized. Love letters. To Dorian. | remembered the girl who wrote them. Young, vibrant, foolishly hopeful. Our marriage, arranged politically between two powerful D.C. families, had been a secret dream for me. | had loved Dorian Miller since | was a teenager, admiring his sharp mind, his quiet intensity, his ambition.

| had believed our union, even if arranged, held the promise of real love, a chance to turn my long-held crush into a true partnership. He was charismatic, brilliant, and utterly captivating. | saw past his less prestigious background, drawn to his raw talent and drive. | was so sure | could make him love me. Even through the five years of brutal, soul-crushing war, a small, stubborn part of me had clung to the ghost of that initial affection, a desperate desire for his approval, his understanding.

The fact that | had never truly let him go, even as | fought him with every fiber of my being, twisted in my gut. | ran my fingers over the faded ink, my own youthful handwriting "Always and forever, Dorian." The words felt like a cruel joke, a relic from another lifetime. These letters, brimming with such naive hope, now seemed like worthless scraps of paper. | moved to discard them. A hand snatched the bundle from my grasp. | spun around. Blake Dominguez stood behind me, swaying slightly, the bundle of letters held loosely in his hand.

His eyes, bloodshot and gleaming, scanned the words, a knowing smirk playing on his lips. Dorian had given him a spare key to the apartment years ago, a casual gesture of trust that had become a tool of torment. 4 "Give me those," | said, my voice flat, devoid of any command. Blake chuckled, a low, unpleasant sound. "Oh, the great Ariana Mcneil. So this is your big secret, huh? All this time, | thought you were playing hard to get, or just a cold bitch. Turns out you were always just desperate for him." He sneered. "Dorian never even looked at these, you know.

He always found your affections pathetic. He preferred Kinsley's quiet devotion, not your... fierce declarations." | remembered Dorian's dismissive glances, his cutting remarks about my "overtures," his constant accusations of my family's manipulative nature, which he always seemed to project onto me. He had never seen my love. He had only seen the Mcneil name, and a tool for his revenge. "What do you want, Blake?" | asked, my voice detached. My eyes were fixed on the bottle in my pocket. He stepped closer, the scent of cheap liquor and stale sweat clinging to him.

He grinned, a lecherous, predatory smile. "What do | want?" he slurred, pulling out his phone. He started recording. "The same thing | wanted on your wedding night, remember? Only this time, there's no Dorian to interrupt our fun, and no scandal for you to hide behind. It's just you and me, Ariana. And everyone will see what a slut you really are." He gestured withhis phone. "For old times' sake, darling." He lunged, pinning me to the bed, his weight crushing me, his triumphantlaughter filling the room. My body went limp, a sudden, complete surrender.

My hand, however, moved with a purpose of its own, teaching into my pocket. My fingers closed around the cold, smooth glass of the pill bottle. And in that moment, | knew exactly what | would take from him before | left this world forever. Dorian Miller POV After dropping Kinsley off at the emergency room for her sprained ankle, Dorian sped back towards the apartment. He gripped the steering wheel, his knuckles white. He had just seen Ariana's deleted contacts, her name erased from his phone. A cold dread, a fear he had never known, seized him. His heart pounded, a frantic drum in his chest.

He burst into the apartment. The front door was ajar. A dark stain on the pristine marble of the entryway steps immediately caught his eye. Blood. His vision narrowed. His breath caught in his throat. The world tilted. His blood ran cold. He sprinted towards the bedroom, kicking the door open with a single, desperate blow. And what he saw inside would haunt him for the rest of his life. For you The Christening That Broke My ... Chapter 5 Dorian Miller POV The sight that greeted me in the bedroom seared itself into my memory, a nightmare | would relive for the rest of my hollow existence. Blake Dominguez lay unconscious on the floor beside the bed, a gaping, bloody wound where his genitals should ave been. A crimson pool spread around him, soaking into the pristine white carpet. Ariana lay on the bed, her eyes half-open, but her pupils were dilated and fixed. A small, empty bottle lay on the nightstand, its label for a powerful sedative and painkiller. White foam and streaks of blood bubbled from her lips.

My legs moved, heavy and disconnected, towards the bed. My hand reached out, trembling, to touch er face. It was cold. So cold. | pulled my hand back, then reached again, pressing two fingers against her neck. No pulse. Nothing. "Ariana?" My voice was a choked whisper, raw and unfamiliar. "Ariana, wake up!" She didn't move. Her head lolled to the side, her body limp and unresponsive. | scooped her into my arms, shaking her, desperately trying to bring her back. "Ariana, open your eyes! Look at me!" | pleaded, my voice cracking. "Hate me! Fight me!

A faint warmth lingered on her skin, a fragile ember of life. That last trace of warmth sent a violent tremor through my body. | fumbled for my phone, my fingers clumsy. | dialed 911, my voice slurred, almost unintelligible "Someone has been... injured," | choked out, forcing thewords throughmy constricted throat. chapters.content:
Chapter 6 Dorian Miller POV Sirens wailed in the distance, growing louder with terrifying speed. Within minutes, the apartment was filled with paramedics. They efficiently lifted Ariana onto a stretcher. | stood rooted to the spot, my hands stained with blood and foam, watching them work. "We have another victim here," a paramedic said, pointing to Blake. "What happened to him?" | looked at Blake, his face pale and contorted in pain. My gaze was empty, devoid of concern. "He'll live," | said, my voice flat, emotionless. | didn't elaborate.

My eyes remained fixed on Ariana, on the pale curve of her neck, the faint rise and fall of her chest, or lack thereof. As they moved her towards the door, | lunged forward, grabbing the side of the stretcher. "I'm coming with her." | stated. my voice firm. In the ambulance, | held Ariana's hand. It was cold, stiff, unresponsive. Her fingers were curled slightly. | gently pried them open, revealing dark smears under her nails. Dirt. And something else, something metallic. The realization hit me like a physical blow.

She had dug at the ground, at the earth of her own grave, in her final moments. She didn't just give up. She had fought to end it. | closed my eyes, a torrent of images flooding my mind. Ariana, drenched in the rain, her eyes vacant, her "just finish it" ringing in my ears. Ariana, calm, asking how | wanted her to apologize, offering humiliation as if it meant nothing. Ariana, her eyes holding that profound, terrifying despair. | had seen it all. | had chosen to ignore it, blinded by my own rage, my own warped sense of justice.

| had seen her walking towards her death, and | had done nothing but push her faster. She truly wanted to die. She wanted to escape me. The fluorescent lights of the emergency room flickered for three agonizing hours. | stood in the corridor, a statue of torment, unable to move, unable to breathe. Every five minutes, | asked a passing doctor or nurse about her condition. No one answered. No one met my gaze. Each silence was a fresh stab of fear. Finally, the head of emergency appeared, his face grim. He stood before me for a long time, saying nothing. "She...

she was too late," he finally said, his voice soft, almost apologetic. "The amount of medication she ingested... there was nothing we could do." | pushed past him, stumbling into the sterile white room. Ariana lay on the operating table, a white sheet pulled over her body. | ripped it back. Her eyes were closed now, peacefully, eternally. The white foam, the crimson streaks, marred her lips. | touched her face again. It was completely cold. No trace of warmth remained. The last ember was gone. All the strength drained from my body. | tried to call her name, but no sound escaped my throat.

| bent over, resting my forehead against her cold shoulder. My body convulsed with silent sobs, my shoulders shaking violently. Five years of hatred, five years of calculated cruelty, all for this. The unspoken questions in her now-still eyes burned into my soul: Why did you betray me? Why didn't you trust me? Why did you never love me? And | had no answers. Only guilt.

chapters.content:
Chapter 7 Dorian Miller POV Inanother emergencyroom, Blake Dominguezawoke. He groaned, his eyes fluttering open. His hand immediately went to his groin. He touched the thick bandages, the agonizing throb. He looked down. Nothing. Just gauze and a searing pain. A guttural scream ripped from his throat, primal and animalistic. "She castrated me! That bitch castrated me!" he shrieked, thrashing against the restraints. "I'll kill her! I'll fucking kill her!" Nurses rushed in, administering a sedative. His screams slowly subsided, his eyes glazed over, staring blankly at the ceiling.

| walked into his room. He saw me, his eyes widening, a flicker of raw fear cutting through the haze of the drugs. Tears welled up in his eyes. "Dorian, my friend," he whimpered, his voice weak. "Look what she did to me! That psycho! You have to avenge me, Dorian! You have to kill her!" He reached out, grabbing my sleeve, his grip desperate. "Please, Dorian, she destroyed me!
